jobs.title: Continuous Improvement Specialist -  Expert
jobs.location: Inver Grove Heights, Minnesota, United States
jobs.description:
CHS Inc. is a leading global agribusiness owned by farmers, ranchers and cooperatives across the United States that provides grain, food and energy resources to businesses and consumers around the world.  We serve agriculture customers and consumers across the United States and around the world.  Most of our employees are in the United States, but today we have employees in 19 countries. At CHS, we are creating connections to empower agriculture.
Summary

CHS, Inc. has an exciting opportunity for an Expert Continuous Improvement (CI) Specialist to join our Continuous Improvement Team (CI) in our Agriculture Division. In this role, you will co-facilitate and co-lead enterprise-wide initiatives that improve business processes, enable cross-functional collaboration, and deliver measurable results aligned with our product line strategies.

This position requires a strong blend of facilitation, project management, and technical problem-solving skills- including the ability to leverage data analytics to optimize processes, increase visibility, and sustain improvements.

This role is based at our corporate headquarters in Inver Grove Heights, MN. This role requires 25–50% travel to operational sites based on business needs.

Responsibilities

Collaboration & Facilitation
- Co-facilitate and co-lead large-scale CI projects with other CI members, partnering closely with all levels of business and functional leaders.
- Partner with Product Line and functional leaders to identify opportunities and ensure alignment with product line strategies.
- Lead value stream mapping sessions, Kaizen events, problem solving workshops, and stakeholder discussions to drive engagement and adoption of improved ways of working.

Process Optimization
- Lead end-to-end process improvement efforts focused on simplifying work, eliminating waste, improving flow and increasing operational effectiveness.
- Apply Lean methodologies (e.g., standard work, root cause analysis, visual management, continuous flow) to improve process performance and consistency.
- Collaborate with ITW and business teams to design and implement practical digital solutions that enable improved processes and reduce manual work.
- Deploy process changes, standardization and low-code solutions to streamline workflows, improve scalability and support long-term sustainability.
- Ensure improvements are embedded into daily operations through standard work, documentation, and leader routines.

Change Management & Project Management
- Lead the planning, execution, and governance of high-priority projects, ensuring delivery on outcomes and timelines.
- Develop project charters, action plans, and progress tracking tools that drive accountability and visibility. Support change management strategies including communication, training, stakeholder readiness, and leadership engagement.
- Serve as a coach and mentor to leaders and employees, fostering a culture of problem-solving and continuous learning.
- Promote adoption and sustainment of CI tools, methodologies, and standardized processes across functions.

Performance Insights and Visual Management
- Use operational data to identify performance gaps, prioritize improvement opportunities and measure the impact of process changes.
- Build and maintain visual management tools (dashboards, scorecards, digital boards) to track progress and sustain improvements.
- Translate operational performance information into clear, actionable insights for leaders and front-line teams.

Minimum Qualifications (required)

- High School diploma or GED
- 7+ years of experience in Continuous Improvement, Operational Excellence, Process Improvement, Data Analytics, Program Management, or related fields.

Additional Qualifications

- Lean or Six Sigma certification (Green Belt, Black Belt, or equivalent)
- Strong background in data analytics and building visual management systems.
- Proven ability to co-lead complex, cross-functional initiatives.
- Strong facilitation, communication, project management, and change management skills.
- Experience using data to support process improvement and visual management
- Agriculture or commodities industry experience is a plus
- Pre-employment screening is based on the job requirements and industry guidelines and may or may not be required for the position. If required, selected candidates must pass pre-employment screenings to include all or a combination of drug, criminal, motor vehicle check, physical requirements, and FMCSA Clearinghouse.

CHS offers a competitive total rewards package. Compensation includes base wage and, depending upon position, may include other earnings such as bonus, incentives and commissions. Actual pay offered will vary based on multiple factors which may include, without limitation, experience, education, training, specialized skills and certifications, minimum wage/salary requirements under local law.

Benefits include medical, dental, vision, wellness programs, life insurance, health and dependent care spending accounts, paid time off, 401(k), pension, profit sharing, short- and long-term disability, tuition reimbursement and adoption assistance, subject to the eligibility requirements for each benefit plan.

CHS is an Equal Opportunity Employer/Veterans/Disability.

Please note that any communication from a CHS recruiter would be sent using a chsinc.com email address. In addition, a CHS recruiter will not ask for confidential information over the phone or in an email, or request money from a candidate involved in an offer process. If you have questions regarding an employment opportunity, please reach out to chscareers@chsinc.com ; to verify that the communication is from CHS.

jobs.title: Director, Supply Chain & Logistics
jobs.location: Inver Grove Heights, Minnesota, United States
jobs.description:
CHS Inc. is a leading global agribusiness owned by farmers, ranchers and cooperatives across the United States that provides grain, food and energy resources to businesses and consumers around the world.  We serve agriculture customers and consumers across the United States and around the world.  Most of our employees are in the United States, but today we have employees in 19 countries. At CHS, we are creating connections to empower agriculture.
Summary

CHS, Inc. has an exciting opportunity within our Transportation and Logistics team for a Director, Supply Chain and Logistics . This leadership role will provide strategic direction and oversight across CHS transportation and logistics, including sales, brokerage, dispatch, carrier sales, account management, pricing, private fleet optimization, and network strategy. The Director will be accountable for integrating commercial and operational capabilities to drive profitable growth, optimize asset and non-asset capacity, improve service and execution, and strengthen CHS’s competitive position in the transportation market.

Responsibilities

- Provide strategic leadership for logistics sales, brokerage, dispatch, carrier sales, pricing, account management, and network optimization functions.
- Support private fleet optimization, balancing service, asset utilization, cost, capacity, and profitability across the transportation network.
- Drive service and execution excellence, establishing consistent operating disciplines and accountability across dispatch, fleet, brokerage, and carrier operations.
- Develop and execute strategies that support profitable growth, operational efficiency, exceptional customer service, and long-term transportation competitiveness.
- Lead the commercialization of the private fleet, identifying opportunities to leverage available fleet capacity to generate incremental third-party revenue and improve overall asset returns.
- Own external customer market pricing strategy, ensuring transportation pricing reflects market conditions, capacity dynamics, service requirements, and targeted profitability.
- Provide strategic leadership for carrier sales, developing and optimizing a high-performing third-party carrier network that expands capacity, improves service, and supports profitable growth.
- Lead transportation customer account management, including customer segmentation, relationship development, service performance, retention, growth opportunities, and overall account profitability.
- Develop and execute an integrated asset vs. non-asset transportation strategy, determining the optimal use of CHS private fleet, dedicated capacity, brokerage, and third-party carriers based on economics, service requirements, seasonality, and network needs.
- Align sales, dispatch, pricing, brokerage, fleet, and account-management activities to ensure consistent communication, streamlined decision-making, and competitive market positioning.
- Establish and monitor key performance indicators across service, cost, asset utilization, revenue, margin, customer performance, carrier performance, and network efficiency to drive continuous improvement.
- Partner with internal stakeholders to identify opportunities for process improvement, network expansion, cost savings, revenue growth, and improved customer experience.
- Evaluate transportation market trends, customer needs, pricing dynamics, and capacity opportunities to support long-term business objectives and inform commercial and operational strategy.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with customers, carriers, and strategic business partners.
- Lead and develop high-performing teams while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, commercial thinking, and operational excellence.
- Support strategic initiatives that enhance organizational agility and improve the ability to respond to seasonal business demands.

Minimum Qualifications (required)

- High School diploma or GED
- 7+ years of experience in transportation, logistics, supply chain, brokerage, or related operational functions
- Prior leadership experience with progressively advancing level of leadership responsibilities

Additional Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree preferred in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Business, Transportation, Operations Management, or related field.
- 10+ years of experience preferred in transportation, logistics, supply chain, brokerage, or related operational functions.
- Entrepreneurial spirit with a desire to lead and inspire a growing team through transformation within a fortune 100 organization.
- Demonstrated experience leading multiple functions and managing complex business operations.
- Strong financial, analytical, and strategic planning capabilities.
- Experience leading transportation sales, brokerage, carrier management, dispatch, and pricing functions.
- Knowledge of fleet operations, carrier network management, and transportation optimization strategies.
- Experience developing and implementing large-scale operational improvement initiatives.
- Strong commercial acumen and understanding of transportation market dynamics.
- Experience leveraging data and technology solutions to improve decision-making and operational performance. Excellent communication, relationship management, negotiation, and leadership skills.
- Experience supporting organizations with significant seasonal fluctuations in transportation demand.

If required, selected candidates must pass pre-employment screenings to include all or a combination of drug, criminal, motor vehicle check, physical requirements and FMCSA Clearinghouse
